channel.title: The Catholic Review - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Catholic Review (catholicreview.org)

item.title: Court allows subpoena of Archdiocese of Seattle in abuse investigation
item.description: A Washington state appeals court has ruled that the state's attorney general can subpoena religious organizations -- including the Archdiocese of Seattle -- for records related to alleged sexual abuse, as part of determining whether charitable funds were used to cover up such actions.

item.title: Religious freedom watchdog annual report spotlights ‘terrifying crisis of religious violence’ in Nigeria
item.description: Nigeria is facing "a terrifying crisis of religious violence," the U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom said in its 2026 annual report, released March 4.

item.title: Drone strike on Iraqi Catholic church complex reopens old wounds
item.description: The Catholic community in northern Iraq has been shaken by the attack of an explosive drone hitting the Chaldean Catholic complex in Ankawa, outside of Irbil.

item.title: Catholic sisters to host livestream prayer for peace as violence continues in Iran, Middle East
item.description: Catholic sisters from around the world are inviting people to join a livestreamed prayer for peace March 6 amid ongoing violence related to the U.S. and Israel-Iran war.

item.title: Beloved Notre Dame coaching legend Lou Holtz remembered for ‘building men, not just players’
item.description: On March 4, Lou Holtz died in Orlando, Fla., at the age of 89, surrounded by his family. Forever etched in Fighting Irish lore for leading Notre Dame to the 1988 National Championship, Holtz leaves behind not just a decorated football resume but a legacy of shaping young men and inspiring people to live virtuously.

item.title: Iran’s exiled Christians watch events unfolding across Middle East with hope, fear
item.description: As conflict flares across the Middle East following U.S. and Israeli attacks on Iran, the country's exiled Christians remain deeply anxious about the future.

item.title: Sudanese bishops express distress at the massacre of 178 people in northern South Sudan
item.description: Catholic bishops in Sudan and South Sudan have expressed distress at the brutal killing of nearly 178 people in northern South Sudan on March 2.

item.title: Lebanon’s Eastern Catholic patriarchs, bishops call for ‘spiral of violence’ to end
item.description: The Assembly of Catholic Patriarchs and Bishops in Lebanon issued a statement March 5 in which they called "for an immediate halt to the spiral of violence" currently taking place in the Middle East and urged "a return to constructive dialogue and responsible diplomatic action, grounded in the pursuit of the common good of peoples who long for a peaceful life founded on justice and dignity."

item.title: Pope Leo XIV prays for leaders to ‘abandon projects of death’ in peace prayer video
item.description: Pope Leo XIV prayed for world leaders to “abandon projects of death” in a video message released by the Vatican on March 5 calling on people around the world to pray for peace.

item.title: With Noem out, Catholic immigration advocates call for change in administration immigration policy
item.description: Catholic immigration advocates are calling for change at the Department of Homeland Security after President Donald Trump announced March 5 that Kristi Noem is leaving her post. President Trump announced that he had chosen Sen. Markwayne Mullin, R-Okla., to replace her as secretary.
